ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in Figure A, two identical wooden blocks A and B, each with a mass of 4 kg, are stacked on a horizontal table. Under the action of a horizontal force $F_{1}$ of 16 N, blocks A and B move together in uniform linear motion. ($g$ is taken as $10 \, \mathrm{N/kg}$)

1. At this moment, what is the magnitude of the frictional force $F_{f1}$ on the upper surface of block B? What is the magnitude of the frictional force $F_{f2}$ on the lower surface of block B?
2. What is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the tabletop and the wooden block?
3. If A and B are placed closely together on a horizontal tabletop (as shown in Figure B) and a horizontal force $F_{2}$ is applied to A to make them move together at a constant velocity, what is the magnitude of the elastic force exerted by A on B?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left in the figure, Figure A shows wooden block A stacked on wooden block B, and B is placed on a horizontal rough tabletop; horizontal force F1 acts on the lower wooden block B and points to the right. On the right in the figure, Figure B shows the two wooden blocks A and B placed side by side in close contact on the same horizontal rough tabletop; horizontal force F2 acts on A and points to the right. Reasoning: In Figure A, A and B together undergo uniform linear motion, so the acceleration is 0. First isolate the upper wooden block A: in the horizontal direction, A can only be subject to the friction force exerted on it by B; since the resultant force on A in the horizontal direction is 0, this friction force is 0. From action force and reaction force, it can be known that the friction force Ff1 received by the upper surface of B is also 0. Then regard A+B as a whole: the only horizontal external forces are F1=16 N to the right and the kinetic friction force exerted by the tabletop on the lower surface of B. The whole moves uniformly, and the resultant force is 0, so the friction force Ff2 received by the lower surface of B is 16 N. The supporting force of the tabletop on the two wooden blocks is N=(4+4)×10=80 N. From f=μN, obtain μ=16/80=0.2. In Figure B, A and B side by side together move uniformly. Isolate wooden block B: the magnitude of the kinetic friction force exerted on B by the tabletop is μmg=0.2×4×10=8 N, and the direction is opposite to the direction of motion. B moves uniformly, and the resultant force in the horizontal direction is 0, so the elastic force exerted by A on B must balance this friction force, with magnitude 8 N. Final answer: Ff1=0 N, Ff2=16 N; μ=0.2; the elastic force exerted by A on B is 8 N.
